artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan adding optional S2_API_KEY support and an ordered OpenAlex/Crossref fallback chain to literature-discover.sh Tier 3 via a shared tier3_emit_record() extraction, with a byte-identical pre/post-refactor regression gate and an end-to-end ingest-bridge verification.

memory_candidates.content: When adding alternative providers/backends behind an existing single-provider code path, sequence the work as extract-then-add, never add-then-unify: first lift the incumbent's per-record normalization, ID derivation, and dedup logic into one shared emit helper and prove the refactor byte-identical against a golden baseline captured before the change, then have each new provider do nothing but map its own response shape onto that helper's parameter list. This makes output-schema identity true by construction rather than by parallel reimplementation, and gives a clean partial-rollback point (refactor kept, providers reverted) if the new backends prove unworkable. Capturing the golden baseline requires a deterministic transport stub -- for shell scripts calling bare `curl`, a PATH-shadowing stub script dispatching on request host is sufficient and needs no code change in the script under test.
